highlights.title: Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China with iOS 27.3
highlights.summary: Apple will launch Apple Intelligence in China with iOS 27.3, the company announced on its Chinese newsroom website, as reported by MacRumors. The Apple Intelligence features will be available first in an iOS 27.3 beta that's set to launch on November 4th, with a full iOS 27.3 release scheduled for…
body: Apple is launching an iOS 27.3 beta next week that will bring some of the initial Apple Intelligence features to the Chinese market.

This launch doesn’t bring the new Siri AI to China. Instead, Apple is launching several of its earlier Apple Intelligence features like notification summaries, real-time translation, rewriting and proofreading tools, visual intelligence, and removing objects from photos. Apple also says it has worked with Ailbaba to add support for its Qwen chatbot in some experiences, which sounds similar to iOS’s integration with OpenAI’s ChatGPT that launched in 2024.
Apple Intelligence was approved in China in July, which signalled that the launch of the AI tools was getting near. Apple trained its own LLM specifically for China, Reuters reported in August.

highlights.title: Leclerc seals Mexico City practice double as Hamilton suffers technical issue
highlights.summary: Charles Leclerc completed a Friday practice double at the Mexico City Grand Prix but Ferrari's strong showing was dampened by Lewis Hamilton suffering a technical issue.
body: Leclerc produced a time of 1:17.827s to finish just over a tenth clear of McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell, with the British pair among 10 drivers who had earlier sat out the opening session to make way for rookie drivers.
Kimi Antonelli, who only needs to finish ninth in Sunday's race to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion, was a tenth down on his team-mate Russell in fourth.
Hamilton had been on course to go fastest as the session approached its midway point before suffering what appeared to be an engine issue in the final sector of his push lap.

He completed the lap but was then swiftly told by his engineer to pull over on track, ending his session early and denying him valuable information that his rivals were able to gather with their race simulations.

highlights.title: The 10 Best Star Trek: The Next Generation Episodes, Ranked
highlights.summary: One of the great things about Star Trek: The Next Generation is that you never quite knew what kind of adventure you were going to get. One week, the Enterprise might be facing an enemy capable of destroying the Federation.
body: That variety was part of the show's appeal. Over seven seasons, The Next Generation could deliver thrilling science-fiction adventures, tackle complicated moral questions, and occasionally make viewers laugh out loud. But what made the series special wasn't just the stories. It was the characters and the relationships that developed among them, giving even the most far-fetched adventures a human connection.

Nearly 40 years after its premiere, the best episodes remain just as enjoyable to revisit. Some are remembered for their ambitious ideas, others for a particular performance, a heartbreaking moment or a perfectly delivered line. Not every episode on this list is flawless, but each has something that makes it unforgettable. And that's a pretty good measure of great Star Trek.

Few Star Trek episodes grab your attention like "Cause and Effect," which opens with the Enterprise exploding. The crew is trapped in a temporal loop that repeatedly ends in the ship's destruction, with each cycle offering clues that something isn't right.

highlights.summary: “6TM,” directed by Karim Akalay and produced by Walid Bekhti, won the New Visions Award for the most promising European project at the Ji.hlava Documentary Film Festival on Friday.
body: The jury said, “With its imaginative blend of magical realism, humor and social relevance, ‘6TM ‘ offers a fresh vision of European cinema. Rooted in lived experience and shaped through co-creation, ‘6TM’ challenges conventional representations and opens up new possibilities for who gets to tell stories, whose voices are heard, and who sees themselves reflected on screen. We believe this approach holds extraordinary promise for the next generation of both audiences and filmmakers, demonstrating how cinema can become more inclusive and participatory.”

The jury was composed of Katrine Kiilgaard, managing director of CPH:DOX in Denmark; Anda Ionescu, managing partner and producer at Tangaj Production in Romania; and Robert Y. Chang, co-producer of American Documentary at POV in the U.S.

The award was presented in cooperation with UPP, which donated an in-kind grant for visual post-production worth about 15,000 Euros, and Soundaquare, which provided sound mixing and a final sound master, with an estimated value of 5,000 Euros.

highlights.title: Flesh-eating screwworms spread to third state and are attacking pets
highlights.summary: For a genuine fright this Halloween, you can turn your gaze to the southern border, where ravenous, flesh-eating maggots are festering and have taken to eating people's pets.
body: This week, the country’s New World Screwworm (NWS) infestation spread to a third state, Arizona, which joins New Mexico and Texas in being plagued by the horrifying parasites. To date, 74 animal cases have been identified in the US since the flies re-invaded the country in June.

The flies lay hundreds of eggs in wounds and moist orifices of animals, and the resulting voracious maggots feast on their victims. The maggots resemble screws and tortuously bore and twist into living flesh, causing severe, sometimes fatal wounds, before dropping to the ground to develop into adults.

Because of their ability to ravage livestock, the flies were eliminated from the country in the 1960s through aerial releases of sterile male flies, which thwart successful breeding. For years, they were held at bay using a biological barrier along the Darién Gap at the border of Panama and Colombia. But the barrier was breached in 2022, and the flies have made their way back to the US through Central America.

highlights.title: Marvin R. Shanken, Longtime Publisher and Editor of Wine Spectator, Dies at 83
highlights.summary: Marvin R. Shanken, the longtime editor and publisher of Wine Spectator magazine who was instrumental in elevating the profile of American wine business, died Thursday in Manhattan. He was 83.
body: Wine Spectator became a key educational tool to help consumers become more familiar with the beverage, and contributed significantly to raising the status of the Napa Valley wine region. Wine Spectator articles utilized the 100 point wine rating system, which made buying fine bottles much more approachable for the general audience.

Shanken also founded the magazine Cigar Aficionado and purchased Food Arts and Malt Advocate, which was renamed Whisky Advocate. Other publications he founded through his M. Shanken Communications include Market Watch and Shanken News Daily.

“He helped educate millions of Americans on the joys and virtues of wine, and tirelessly encouraged and pushed winemakers to produce the best for their customers,” Wine Spectator wrote in its obituary.

Among his many milestones were establishing Wine Spectator’s Restaurant Awards program, taking over the long-running Wine Experience weekend to bring producers together with consumers and creating the Wine Spectator Scholarship Foundation.

highlights.title: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
highlights.summary: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable.
body: The new control will allow publishers to apply their AI training preferences across multiple crawlers.

The shared “policy token” signal is proposed by Kevin Kelley, a technical lead for standards at Anthropic, as part of the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF). It will live within a website’s robots.txt file, which has long signaled which web crawlers can and can’t scrape a site — whether for search indexing, archiving, or AI training. Currently, sites have to signal their AI training preferences separately to each AI company.

The announcement comes as publishers grapple with the continuing influx of AI crawlers scraping their sites and feeding their content into AI models. Some companies and organizations have attempted to combat unauthorized scraping, with the Really Simple Licensing (RSL) standard giving publishers the ability to charge crawlers that visit their sites, and Cloudflare blocking AI crawlers by default.

highlights.title: Cate Blanchett-Backed Group and Collection of Hollywood Stars File Brief in New York Times-OpenAI Lawsuit: Hollywood Has ‘Proven Infrastructure’ to License Content
highlights.summary: The Human Consent Foundation, the Cate Blanchett-backed nonprofit trying to protect the likenesses of individuals from unauthorized scraping by AI models, and a legion of Hollywood companies have filed an amicus brief in the New York Times’ lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming the tech…
body: “Defendants have argued that licensing creative works for AI training is cost-prohibitive,” the brief read. “Defendants also claim there is no settled means of valuing training data. The facts demonstrate otherwise. The creative industries already have in place a proven infrastructure and workflows to clear rights for dispersed works at scale and cost-effectively.”

In a statement, HCF co-founder and CEO Nikki Hexum said the filing was intended to show the court “how the creative industry actually works and acknowledge the solutions that have been built and are continuing to develop for this new digital era.”

“Our goal is to ensure that as the market for AI data licensing grows, the humans who create the value in that market are protected and have a meaningful choice,” Hexum added. “We are not starting from scratch. There is already a functioning market and infrastructure for licensing creative work. We just need to ensure that new AI technology respects those boundaries and choices, including the choice not to participate.”

highlights.title: Supersonic airliner in doubt as company shifts to powering AI data centers
highlights.summary: Boom Supersonic CEO Blake Scholl recently declared “it’s time for a renaissance in energy and in supersonic flight” as the supersonic airliner company unveiled a Colorado factory dedicated to making gas turbines for AI data centers.
body: One of the company’s first customers, United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby, has expressed doubts about Boom’s original plan to deliver the first Overture supersonic airliner in 2029. Kirby’s latest frank assessment came during an interview with the Office Hours: Business Edition podcast that appeared on October 28, 2026.
“‘29 is their official timeline,” Kirby told podcast host Monica Langley. “It’s not going to happen in ‘29—it’s going to take longer.”

Boom first made headlines for flying its XB-1 demonstrator aircraft in 2024 and 2025 to demonstrate a “boomless cruise” concept that harnesses the Mach cutoff phenomenon. Such a feat involves flying just beyond supersonic speeds at higher altitudes under specific atmospheric conditions, so that the aircraft’s shockwaves refract upward and minimize the impact on the ground.

The company’s plan to revive supersonic air travel has been backed by the Trump administration via efforts to ease regulations. In June 2026, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposed a new rule overturning a long-standing ban on commercial supersonic flights over the United States, following an executive order from President Donald Trump.

body: Five MIT faculty members and two additional alumni were recently named to the 2026 cohort of AI2050 Fellows. The honor is announced annually by Schmidt Sciences, Eric and Wendy Schmidt’s philanthropic initiative that aims to accelerate scientific innovation.

Conceived and co-chaired by Eric Schmidt and James Manyika, AI2050 is a philanthropic initiative aimed at helping to solve hard problems in artificial intelligence. Within their research, each fellow will contend with the central motivating question of AI2050: “It’s 2050. AI has turned out to be hugely beneficial to society. What happened? What are the most important problems we solved and the opportunities and possibilities we realized to ensure this outcome?”
MIT alumni Irene Chen PhD '22 and Allison Z. Koenecke '14 as well as former postdoc Juan Carlos Perdomo were also named AI2050 Early Career Fellows.

Alex de Minaur has enjoyed a landmark 350th tour-level win of his career at the Vienna Open, downing an old rival to set up a semi-final date with the world…
body: Australia’s main man defeated Matteo Berrettini, the Italian he’s had plenty of trouble with down the years, for the second successive year in the quarter-final of the ATP 500 event at the Wiener Stadthalle.

Not only did his 7-6 (7-4) 6-2 triumph set “Demon” up for a third duel in just over a month with Zverev on Saturday but it boosted his bid to reach the season-ending men’s championship, the ATP Finals, which still lies in the balance.

World No 10 de Minaur found a way to draw first blood in a tight first stanza after saving a set point at 5-6, going on to take control of the tiebreak when the Italian, almost criminally, plonked a simple put-away into the net.

De Minaur crucially saved a couple of break points at the start of the next set and cashed in by himself breaking Berrettini for the first time in the next game when the Italian produced an embarrassing air-shot when faced with a straightforward smash.

highlights.title: New Pokémon Release Brings Hundreds of New Eeveelutions
highlights.summary: With eight official Eeveelutions, fans of the beloved normal-type Pokémon aren't hurting for options — yet paradoxically, they're also one of the most neglected segments of the fandom. After all, it's been 13 years since Game Freak introduced a new Eevee monster in Pokémon X and Pokémon Y.
body: Pokémon Winds and Waves could potentially introduce a new Eevee, but that game doesn't seem to be coming out any time soon. Rather than get their hopes up for something that is extremely unlikely, though, Eevee devotees might be better served by playing a new fan game called Pokémon Oops! All Eevees.

Despite the name, the fan game isn't a one-trick Ponyta. Yes, every monster in the game has been replaced with an Eeveelution, but creator 999999999 has also introduced all sorts of original Eevee designs into the experience as well. There's a ghost-type Eevee called Fanteon, a flying-type creature called Aeraerieon, and a fighting-type Eeveelution called Aercampeon, just to name a few. The fan game isn't afraid to double-dip into existing Eeveelution types, either. Many of these new designs have their own evolution lines.

All told, Oops! All Eevees introduces an astonishing 326 Eeveelutions into the base Pokémon FireRed game. A video that quickly speeds through all the available monsters in this fan game runs nearly 40 minutes.

highlights.title: Q&A: Hey AI, who should I vote for this year?
highlights.summary: MIT professors Adam Berinsky and Chara Podimata discuss a new project to track how AI chatbots are responding to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.
body: People are peppering artificial intelligence chatbots everyday with questions, but when it comes to politics and the looming 2026 U.S. midterm elections, what role are AI platforms playing? Could an AI chatbot sway a voter to switch parties or re-examine their political beliefs?

MIT researchers have built a new dashboard, called the LLM Election Observatory, to examine, in real-time, how popular AI chatbots are responding to questions about the 2026 midterm elections. The team behind the dashboard — led by Professor Adam Berinsky, Assistant Professor Chara Podimata, and Professor Charles Stewart III — has extensive experience studying voting and election administration, AI and misinformation, and how AI systems are impacting human decision making. In an effort to better understand how AI is shaping the election, they designed the dashboard to simulate how individuals across the country communicate with chatbots.

highlights.summary: As a franchise spanning video games, books, and a television series, The Witcher owes everything to 300-year-old fairy tales. The very first book, The Last Wish (which itself is a collection of short stories set in The Witcher universe), has a number of fairy tale references, including "A Grain of…
body: These inspirations continue through The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, widely considered to be one of the best RPGs of all time. The third game in the series by CD Projekt Red famously raised the bar for the quality of its side quests, and there are two that truly embody that fairy tale formula, albeit with much darker themes.

First up, and by far the most memorable of the pair as it's from the base game, is "Ladies of the Wood." If you've played The Witcher 3, you'll recall the Crones of Crookback Bog; a trio of witches who live in the swamp, known as the Weavess, Brewess, and Whispess. They are, for all intents and purposes, grotesque as hell. The three are sisters and daughters of the original Lady of the Wood, whose spirit lives beneath an ancient oak tree nearby, after the Crones killed her.

highlights.title: Where to Eat, Stay, and Play on Easter Island, the Wild, Remote Island in the Pacific
highlights.summary: Also known as Easter Island, this Polynesian isle has long been an aspirational destination—here's how to visit.
body: Today, this Chilean territory is essentially an open-air archaeological museum, with many of its enigmatic moai (representations of Polynesian ancestors) returned to their upright positions following seven decades of restoration. Of course to see Rapa Nui only through its superhuman past is to miss much of the story: The island’s distinct Polynesian culture remains a vital presence, particularly in its sole town, Hanga Roa, where nights come alive with cheerful ukulele music and hip-swirling dances. There’s also a vast, vibrant sea, windswept volcanic plains, and a food culture that draws on the island’s rich heritage and maritime setting.
As a repeat visitor to the island, this is my guide to Rapa Nui.

highlights.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
highlights.summary: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident.
body: “It was a supply-chain compromise where the attacker gained access to the official distribution channel,” Phorian CTO and co-founder Luke Roberts told Ars. “The malicious version 2.1.313 was posted to the official Anthropic account, effectively superseding 2.1.312. Extensions auto-update in Cursor by default, but users can configure this in settings.” Phorian has more details here.
Anthropic has yet to issue public notice of the incident to customers.

Cursor said that the malicious extension attempts to install a persistent SSH backdoor using an added attacker-controlled SSH key, enabling the local SSH service, and opening a reverse SSH tunnel. The code was written to work on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Because Cursor extensions run with the permissions of the tool’s Integrated Development Environment, the backdoored version likely would gain access to local files, source code, and developer tooling once it was installed.

Phorion said the theft of variable names allowed the operator to quickly take inventory of cloud credentials and API tokens stored on a compromised device, likely so it could prioritize which machines to target in follow-up attacks.

body: The debate around Estêvão’s role gathered momentum this week, with the noise growing after the 19-year-old watched as an unused substitute as Alonso’s side lost to Liverpool on penalties in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. The Brazilian became an instant hit with Chelsea fans after joining from Palmeiras last year and there are fears that the winger could look to leave after starting twice in 11 games in all competitions this season.

Yet while Estêvão is having a tougher time during his second year in English football, Alonso insisted that the Brazil international is part of his plans and will not be loaned out to get more games in January.

“No discussions about that,” Alonso said. “It’s no secret that all players want to be on the pitch. When any of them haven’t had enough minutes because of my decision, I have to take the responsibility for that. But everyone has to be ready because in any game they could be important. Este, his training and his attitude has been good.”

body: It's a clarification that arrived after Deane posted a community message for Destiny fans yesterday. The message, featured as part of a lengthy Q&A blog post, outlined the unvaulting process for Destiny 2 content that was previously promised last month, but one segment left players confused – and concerned – about the future and extraction shooter Marathon's role in the big picture.

"We're not going to forget the mistakes of the past, but it's time to learn from them and unify as one Bungie community," the section in question said. "For us, the majority of our Bungie team is legacy Destiny, and we will all tell you that nothing can help bridge us into future more than for Marathon to rapidly evolve and become sustainable. As we head into our December and March updates for Marathon, it’s a formative period for all of us here at Bungie that will help determine the shape of our future, so please encourage each other and know that your support gives our team the energy to finish the fight."

body: When asked about potentially collaborating with Fielder, the “Obsession” director revealed he’s already floated the idea to him: “I told him that. I said, ‘Hey!’ … I just put it out in the water.”

“You Can See Everything” blurs the line between narrative and documentary storytelling and, as Variety’s chief awards editor Clayton Davis puts it, has “turned the movie landscape topsy-turvy.” Much like Barker’s “Obsession,” the film has left the industry re-examining what kinds of movies resonate with Gen Z audiences — and, more importantly, what drives them out to the theaters.
“It felt new, fresh, different,” Barker said of “You Can See Everything.” “You almost can’t even call it a documentary, but it totally is. I’m just a huge fan of what [Fielder] is doing.”
Barker should have plenty more chances to cross paths with Fielder on the awards circuit, as both their films continue to earn recognition alongside some of the year’s most acclaimed films.
